DITA KNOWLEDGE (retrieval bundle):
[1] imagemap: <imagemap> creates clickable regions (hotspots) over an image, enabling navigation to different topics or resources. It is a utilities-domain specialization of <fig>.

Structure: <imagemap> → <image> (required first child) → <area> (one or more clickable regions)
Each <area> contains: <shape> → <coords> → <xref>

Shape types (same as HTML 4.1 image maps):
- rect — rectangle: coords="left,top,right,bottom"
- circle — circle: coords="centerX,centerY,radius"
- poly — polygon: coords="x1,y1,x2,y2,..
---
[2] dita_spec: from their parent or sibling topics.
The rules for topic nesting can be configured in a document-type shells. For example, the standard DITA
configuration for concept topics only allows nested concept topics. However, local configuration of the
concept topic type could allow other topic types to nest or disallow topic nesting entirely. In addition, the
@chunk attribute enables topics to be equally re-usable regardless of whether they are separate or nested.
The standard DITA configuration for di
---
[3] reltable: <reltable> (relationship table) defines cross-linking relationships between topics in a map. It's the preferred way to create related-topic links without embedding links inside topics.

What is <reltable>?
Instead of adding <xref> or <related-links> inside topics (which creates tight coupling), reltables define relationships centrally in the map. This keeps topics self-contained and reusable.

Structure:
- Each row (<relrow>) defines a set of related topics
- Each cell (<relcell>) contains topic
---
[4] tgroup: <tgroup> is the main structural container inside a CALS <table>. It defines columns, headers, and body rows.

What is <tgroup>?
In the CALS table model (used by DITA's <table> element), <tgroup> wraps the column specifications, optional header, and table body. A <table> can have multiple <tgroup> elements, though one is typical.

Full CALS table structure:
```xml
<table>
  <title>CALS Table Example</title>
  <tgroup cols="3">
    <colspec colname="c1" colwidth="1*"/>
    <colspec colname="c2" co
---
[5] choicetable_vs_simpletable_vs_table: Comparison: <choicetable> vs <simpletable> vs <table> vs <properties> — the four DITA table types.

| Feature | choicetable | simpletable | table (CALS) | properties |
|---------|------------|-------------|--------------|------------|
| Purpose | Present choices in a task step | Simple data table | Full-featured table | Property/parameter reference |
| Context | Inside <step> only | Any body content | Any body content | Inside <refbody> only |
| Columns | Always 2 (option + description) | Any nu
---
[6] dita_spec: and <entry>.
@rowheader
Indicates whether the entries in the respective column SHOULD be considered row headers. Allowable values are:
firstcol
Indicates that entries in the first column of the table are functionally row headers (analogous to the way that a
<thead> element provides column headers). Applies when @rowheader is used on the <table> element.
headers
Indicates that entries of a column described using the <colspec> element are functionally row headers (for
cases with more than one colu
---
[7] dita_spec: attributes defined in this group. These attributes are not available for the <simpletable> elements.
@align
Describes the alignment of text in a table column. Allowable values are:
left
Indicates left alignment of the text.
right
Indicates right alignment of the text.
center
Indicates center alignment of the text.
justify
Justifies the contents to both the left and the right.
char
Use the character specified on the @char attribute for alignment.
-dita-use-conref-target
See Using the -dita-use-co
---
[8] colspec: <colspec> defines properties for a single column in a CALS <table>. Place one <colspec> per column inside <tgroup>, before <thead> and <tbody>.
